budget_seconds.description: Per-request retrieval wall-clock budget override (seconds). None = the server's interactive default (AGENT_QUERY_BUDGET_SECONDS, 20s). For offline/batch callers — eval harnesses, SDK batch jobs — that prefer completeness over latency.

cost_sensitivity.description: Cost preference: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'. When None it is resolved via the request -> consumer-registry -> persisted COST_SENSITIVITY chain (app.services.request_policy.resolve_cost_sensitivity, E1 CR-028). Retrieval ranking itself is not cost-routed; the resolved value steers LLM model selection on the chat/generation paths.

skip_cache.title: Skip Cache

strict_domains.description: When True, disables cross-domain affinity bleed. None = use consumer default.

FieldMappings.description:
Declares how to extract canonical fields from an arbitrary payload dict.

Each value is a dotted-path string (optionally with ``[]`` for array
fan-out) into the incoming ``payload``.  Only ``content`` and
``source_uri`` are required; the others default gracefully.

content.description: Dotted path to the main text content.  Use ``highlights[].text`` to fan-out one item per array element.
content.title: Content

id.description: Optional dotted path to an external ID.  When absent, the ID is derived from ``source_uri``.
id.title: Id

source_uri.description: Dotted path to the canonical URI / URL for this item.
source_uri.title: Source Uri

tags.description: Optional dotted path to a list[str] of tags.  Resolved value must be a Python list; absent path → empty list.
tags.title: Tags

title.description: Optional dotted path to a human-readable title string.
title.title: Title

ts.description: Optional dotted path to an ISO-8601 timestamp.  Defaults to current UTC time when absent or unresolvable.
ts.title: Ts

FieldMappings.title: FieldMappings

mode.description: Verification depth. ``fast`` extracts claims and returns them marked ``status='uncertain'`` with ``verification_skipped=True`` — ~ms latency, no NLI calls, useful for post-fact annotations. ``thorough`` (default) runs the full cross-model NLI pipeline.

HallucinationMode.description:
Verification depth for ``/agent/hallucination``.

Class invariant: post-fact annotation handlers shouldn't make every
caller pay full NLI cost. Each mode is a distinct point on the
cost/quality curve, exposed explicitly so callers don't burn 60-100s
waiting on cross-model verification when a 2s heuristic is enough.
HallucinationMode.title: HallucinationMode

claims.description: Verified claims with status, confidence, and source info
claims.title: Claims

mode.description: Verification depth that was actually applied. ``fast`` returns extracted claims with status='uncertain' and ``nli_skipped=true`` without paying NLI cost; ``thorough`` runs the full cross-model pipeline. Set on the request via ``HallucinationCheckRequest.mode``.
mode.title: Mode

nli_skipped.description: True when cross-model NLI verification was skipped (fast mode). Consumers can use this to decide whether to display a hedged warning vs. an authoritative verdict.
nli_skipped.title: Nli Skipped

reason.description: Reason verification was skipped, if applicable
reason.title: Reason

skipped.description: True if verification was skipped (response too short or no claims)
skipped.title: Skipped

summary.description: Verification summary: per-status counts plus assessed count and the float overall_confidence.
summary.title: Summary

SDKLLMCompleteRequest.description:
Request for ``POST /sdk/v1/llm/complete`` — smart-routed LLM completion.

Consumers describe the task; the smart_router selects the appropriate
model tier (FREE / CHEAP / CAPABLE / RESEARCH / EXPERT) based on
task_type, complexity, and cost_sensitivity. Falls back to Ollama
when available and suitable.

cost_sensitivity.description: Cost preference: low (cheapest) | medium | high (best quality)
cost_sensitivity.title: Cost Sensitivity

query.description: Optional query summary for the router's complexity classifier
query.title: Query

slo_budget_ms.description: Optional wall-clock budget in milliseconds. The smart_router filters tiers by their empirical p95 latency profile; if no tier fits the budget the response is HTTP 503 with a Retry-After header carrying the floor p95. Lets fast-path consumers (e.g. trading-agent) fail-fast and route to direct providers instead of waiting on a slow tier.
slo_budget_ms.title: Slo Budget Ms

task_type.description: Task category: chat | internal | verification | classification | research. Clients may also pass custom values (e.g. 'gtm_creative', 'agent_phase_2'); unknown values map to safe internal routing.
task_type.title: Task Type

SDKLLMCompleteRequest.title: SDKLLMCompleteRequest

estimated_cost_per_1k.description: Estimated cost in USD per 1K tokens (0 for free / Ollama)
estimated_cost_per_1k.title: Estimated Cost Per 1K

provider.description: Routing provider label: ollama | quenchforge | openrouter_paid (legacy openrouter_free stamp removed by CR-027 cost honesty)
provider.title: Provider

tier_p95_ms.description: Empirical p95 wall-clock for the tier this call was routed to. 0 when the tier has no measured profile yet. Useful for client-side adaptive timeout tuning.
tier_p95_ms.title: Tier P95 Ms

Returned from ``POST /sdk/v1/memory/extract`` when the request was
enqueued for background processing. Callers poll

SDKMemoryExtractJobStatus.description:
Status envelope for ``GET /sdk/v1/memory/extract/jobs/{job_id}``.

``status`` transitions: ``queued → started → finished`` (success) or
``queued → started → failed`` (worker error). ``result`` is populated
only when ``status='finished'``; ``error`` is populated only when
``status='failed'``.

error.description: Worker exception summary — populated only when status='failed'

result.description: Worker output — populated only when status='finished'

started_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the worker began processing
started_at.title: Started At

status.description: Job lifecycle state — one of: queued | started | finished | failed | deferred | scheduled | canceled | unknown
status.title: Status

post.description: Accept an arbitrary JSON payload from any external service and ingest its content into the Cerid knowledge base.  The caller supplies a ``field_mappings`` config that declares how to extract canonical fields (content, source URI, timestamp, tags, title, external ID) from the raw ``payload``.  A single payload can map to N ingest items via array fan-out (e.g. ``highlights[].text``).  The ``source_type`` label is stored as provenance metadata and is never branched on in code — this endpoint is generic and not special-cased for any particular service.  See ``docs/INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md`` for per-service mapping examples (Readwise, Pocket, Instapaper, Raindrop, Telegram-bot).

post.description:
Accepts a short audio clip (WAV / WebM / M4A — anything ffmpeg can decode), transcribes it with the bundled whisper.cpp pipeline, and ingests the transcript as an artifact linked to a voice_note Source.

Recommended clip length: 30 s – 5 min. Larger clips should route through the Meeting Capture pipeline (``/meetings``) instead.

Generic inbound endpoint for any external service. The ``{token}`` path segment identifies a previously-created webhook-kind Source record whose ``config`` carries the matching token + optional HMAC secret. Returns ``202 Accepted`` immediately and queues the payload for async processing.

**Authentication:** the token itself is the credential. For higher assurance, configure an HMAC secret on the source and require ``X-Cerid-Signature: sha256=<hex>`` on every request; mismatched signatures return 401.

**Adapter routing:** payloads can carry the canonical fields directly OR the source's config can declare per-source ``field_mappings`` (Readwise / Pocket / Slack / GitHub-events / etc.) that extract them from a third-party-shaped payload.

Tier-aware LLM completion. Consumers describe the task (`task_type`, `cost_sensitivity`); the smart_router selects the best model from FREE / CHEAP / CAPABLE / RESEARCH / EXPERT tiers, preferring Ollama when available. Returns content plus the model actually used and an estimated cost-per-1K-tokens for budget tracking.

post.description:
Extract facts, decisions, and preferences from conversation text and store as KB artifacts. Deduplicates against existing memories.

When ``MEMORY_QUEUE_MODE=async`` is set on the server (and a worker is running), the default behaviour is **fire-and-forget**: returns ``202 Accepted`` immediately with a ``job_id`` and a ``status_url``. Poll ``GET /sdk/v1/memory/extract/jobs/{job_id}`` for the result.

Pass ``?wait=true`` to force the synchronous path (waits for the full extract → consolidate → store pipeline before responding) — use for callers that need the result envelope inline.
